# Homepage patterns for `deadreckon`

## What each site actually does

**bun.sh** — Hero with two-tab install (mac/linux + windows), then leads almost entirely with **benchmark bar charts** (4 of them). Features as a tabbed code-block carousel (11 tabs, one per API). No terminal screenshots, no video. Comparison tables (Bun vs Node vs Deno) carry trust. Social proof: scrolling tweets + logo bar of users.

**deno.com** — "Uncomplicate JavaScript" + dinosaur illustration. Install in a card. Trust = logo wall (Slack, Netlify, Stripe, BofA). Long-form sections, not a card grid. One text-only req/sec stat — no charts.

**vite.dev** — "The Build Tool for the Web." Multi-package-manager tabs. Four feature cards (Instant / HMR / Rich / Optimized). Stars + downloads number prominently. Testimonials from named framework creators (not company logos).

**biomejs.dev** — "Format, lint, and more in a fraction of a second." Install commands inline inside each feature section, not in hero. Before/after code transformation is the load-bearing visual. Three sequential sections, no card grid.

**charm.land** — "We make the command line glamorous." Pure brand-forward; **no install commands on the homepage**. Mascots and playful tags carry everything. Individual repos (gum, glow, lazygit) lean on **animated GIFs** — one per feature, captioned with keybindings.

**oxc.rs** — Tagline + benchmark numbers (26.3ms vs 130.1ms). Six equal-weight tool cards. No install command on the homepage at all — pushes you to docs.

**astral.sh / docs.astral.sh/uv** — Astral's marketing page is brand+testimonials, no install. The **uv docs landing** is the real homepage: tagline, install card, benchmark chart with light/dark variants, terminal-output blocks for each verb (init / add / run / tool).

**prisma.io** — "Postgres, perfectly managed." `npx prisma init` shown as a code snippet next to a "Create database" button. Five illustrated feature cards. Heavy testimonials.

**supabase CLI page** — Pure docs-style: sequential code blocks for install → init → start. No visuals. Honest about being a quickstart, not a marketing page.

**nushell.sh** — Three pillars ("Cross-platform / Everything is data / Powerful plugins"). Static terminal screenshots of `ls`, `fetch`, a typed error. No benchmarks.

**helix-editor.com** — "A post-modern text editor." One button. Six text-only feature sections. No screenshots at all — confident minimalism, but only works because the audience already knows what a modal editor looks like.

**lazygit / gum / glow** — Animated GIFs do all the work. Lazygit has 10 GIFs, each captioned with the workflow and the keybinding. This is the strongest pattern for TUI tools.

## Patterns to steal vs avoid

**Steal:**
- Lazygit's **one-GIF-per-capability** with caption (attach, undo turn, gate signing — each begs to be a 6-sec asciinema).
- Biome's **before/after** framing (transcript-blob → reviewable artifact is a perfect visual).
- Bun/uv **benchmark-as-hero** — but for deadreckon the chart should be "unattended hours survived" or "% of runs with a forgery-resistant gate," not speed.
- Deno's **named-company logo wall** if/when you have one. Otherwise skip.
- Bun's **comparison table** (Bun vs Node vs Deno). Your README's "Compared with Agentic CLIs" table already drafts this — lift it onto the page.
- Charm's tone discipline — name the tool's voice and stick to it.

**Avoid:**
- The tired **"Fast / Simple / Powerful"** three-card grid (Vite gets away with it on brand equity; you won't).
- Astral.sh-style **brand page with no install command** — fine for a company, wrong for a single CLI.
- Helix's no-screenshot minimalism — works for an editor people already imagine; doesn't work for a novel concept like "signed acceptance gate."
- Prisma-style **illustrated feature cards** with no terminal anywhere. Reads as SaaS, not as a CLI you can trust unattended.
- Long testimonial carousels before a working demo.

## Recommended sections (7)

**1. Hero — claim + install + one CTA.**
- Tagline: keep the README's spine — *"A harness around the agent CLI you already use, so you can actually walk away."* Sub: *"Isolated worktrees, signed acceptance gates, durable state, undo, audit trail."*
- Install command in a tabbed block (cargo / homebrew / curl), single primary CTA "Read the docs," secondary "GitHub."
- One short asciinema directly under it: `deadreckon done` → `deadreckon run` → close laptop → `deadreckon attach latest`. This is your bun-benchmark equivalent.

**2. The four-line demo (load-bearing visual).**
Code+output split, à la uv docs. Show the literal README quickstart with real terminal output, including the run id and attach line. Don't animate this one — let people copy it.

**3. The mental model diagram.**
Lift the ASCII flow from the README (`your repo → worktree → turn loop → dr-gate → artifact`) but render it as a clean SVG. Helix-style minimalism works here because the diagram itself is the explanation. This is the section that earns trust for "supervises other CLIs."

**4. Capabilities — five long-form sections, each with one asciinema.**
Not a card grid. One scrollable section per capability, lazygit-style:
- *Isolated worktree* — show `run` creating the dr/... branch, your checkout untouched.
- *Walk-away attach* — split terminal: left runs, right `attach latest` from a fresh shell.
- *Signed acceptance gate* — show `dr-gate` rejecting a forged marker. This is the section nobody else can show; make it the strongest visual on the page.
- *Undo a single turn* — `undo --turn 3`, before/after `git status`.
- *Audit artifact* — render `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` next to a chat-transcript blob, biomejs-style before/after.

**5. "Compared with running the agent CLI directly."**
Lift the README's comparison table verbatim. Bun-style. This is the section that disambiguates deadreckon from Claude Code/Codex/Cursor without picking a fight.

**6. Providers it supervises.**
Logo row: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, Anthropic API, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible. Caption: *"Bring the CLI you already trust. deadreckon owns the boundary, not the intelligence."* Frames the product as additive, not competitive.

**7. Try-it-without-keys + footer.**
The README's `--smoke` block, verbatim. Lets someone validate the loop in 30 seconds with no commitment. Then footer: docs links, status (alpha), GitHub, license.

**Sections to deliberately skip** for v1: testimonial carousel (you don't have named users yet — forced quotes look weak), pricing (OSS), team/about (a CLI doesn't need an About page), three-pillar "Why deadreckon" cards (the comparison table does that job better).

## Key takeaway

Your single highest-leverage visual is **the dr-gate forgery rejection**. Nobody else in this space can show that demo, and it's the one image that makes the rest of the value prop (walk away, trust the result) credible. Build the homepage around that asset and treat everything else as supporting cast.

## Files referenced
- /Users/gdc/deadreckon/README.md (source of taglines, comparison table, mental-model diagram, quickstart block)

# Deadreckon homepage claim audit

## 1. One-sentence positioning (≤15 words)

**"Walk away from your coding agent. Come back to a signed, auditable artifact — not a transcript."**

(13 words. Avoids "the X for Y." Foregrounds the unique mechanic — the signed artifact — and the unique experience — leaving.)

## 2. Five strongest, most-specific claims (each with proof)

1. **"The agent process literally cannot mark its own work done."** A separate binary `dr-gate` reads a UUID nonce from `<run_root>/gate/nonce` that the sandboxed agent process has no read access to, hashes it with the marker fields, and writes the signed `AcceptanceMarker` to `proofs/turn-acceptance.json`. The main binary refuses to promote a run without a valid signature. **Proof:** `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs` (33-line standalone binary), `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:704-720` (`marker_signature`), `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md` §13. **Caveat to flag honestly:** the "signature" is a `DefaultHasher` over the nonce + fields, not a cryptographic MAC. The security property is process isolation of the nonce file, not crypto. The README says "the agent cannot forge the signature" — true under the sandbox boundary, but don't oversell it as crypto.

2. **"Attach the live TUI from a different terminal, on a different day."** Run state is durable on disk; `deadreckon attach latest` polls `events.jsonl`, `spend.jsonl`, `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl`, and provider-native JSONL every 500ms. Same-process attaches use a `tokio::sync::broadcast` `RunEventBus`; cross-process attaches replay `events.jsonl` incrementally. **Proof:** `docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md` §18.3, `crates/deadreckon-core/src/events.rs`.

3. **"Watch acceptance checks stream live — `running 2/5 → passed 2/5 → failed cargo test` — while the watchdog evaluates."** `dr-gate` appends a state transition per check to `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl`; the TUI's acceptance meter colorizes it. **Proof:** `crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:228-244`, AS-BUILT §13.5.

4. **"Undo turn 7 without rolling back turns 1–6 or touching your git history."** Each turn snapshots the working directory under `snapshots/turn-<N>/`; `deadreckon undo --run X --turn 3` restores from that trail, independent of git, and records the undo in `traces.jsonl`. **Proof:** README §"Undo A Single Bad Turn", AS-BUILT §22, `artifacts.rs::snapshot_working`.

5. **"Use Claude Code or Codex without an API key — your subscription drives the loop."** `cli:claude-code` shells `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p` and `cli:codex` shells `codex --ask-for-approval never exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox <mode>`, both inside deadreckon's outer Seatbelt/bwrap sandbox. Spend caps switch to wall-clock for subscription routes. **Proof:** `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_claude_code.rs`, `cli_codex.rs`, AS-BUILT §10.

## 3. Three hero commands

```bash
deadreckon done "users can sign up, log in, and save a drawing"
deadreckon run  "build the app" --max-wall-seconds 1800
deadreckon attach latest
```

These tell the full story in three lines: declare done in English, walk away with a cap, come back later.

## 4. Most compelling visual artifact

**Producible now, lowest-effort, highest-signal:** record `deadreckon attach` against a real smoke run and capture the four-panel TUI (header / spend+context+acceptance meters / tool-call stream / live-files + PIDs). The acceptance meter ticking `running 2/5 → passed 5/5` while the `dr-gate` line scrolls in the activity stream is the single screenshot that explains the product.

**Existing assets on disk:**
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/demo.cast`, `demo-codebase.cast`, `demo-self-documenting.cast` — real asciinema casts from the live `cli:codex` path (DESIGN.md confirms `demo.cast` is real release-binary output). Embed via asciinema-player.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png` — existing logo.
- Real `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` sample at `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/library/build-a-full-ms-paint-ty-abe8d920/567f47b614c944beba64b76930255ef1/docs/RUN-NARRATIVE.md` — use a snippet as a "you get this, not a chat log" inline panel.

**What to fabricate:** a worktree-layout diagram showing `your-repo/` untouched next to `~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<run-id>/` on a `dr/...` branch with `state.json`, `snapshots/turn-N/`, `proofs/turn-acceptance.json`, `events.jsonl` — the file tree is the product.

## 5. Three competitor anchors

- **Claude Code / Codex CLI**: "Same agent, but it runs in its own worktree, snapshots every turn, and can't declare itself done." (Use their name — the user already pays for them; deadreckon is the harness around them, not a replacement.)
- **`tmux` + `nohup` for long agent runs**: "Reattach is a feature of the run, not the terminal. Kill your laptop, attach from a phone-tethered Mac tomorrow — the run state is on disk."
- **`git worktree` + manual scripting**: "deadreckon is what you'd build if you took worktrees seriously: spend caps, snapshots, a signed gate, normalized telemetry, and `apply`/`abandon`/`export` as first-class verbs."

## 6. Three things to NOT put on the homepage

1. **`deadreckon import` from claude/codex/cursor histories.** README sells it as "Cross-Tool State Sharing" but AS-BUILT §16 admits it's "inventory-level" — produces a listing/summary, doesn't deeply normalize. First-time visitors will try it expecting magic and get a flat dump. Save it for the docs.
2. **Chains (`deadreckon chain plan ... --n 4`).** Powerful but cognitively expensive; it implies the user should pre-decompose work, which contradicts the "write 'done' in English, walk away" pitch. Mention it once in a "for bigger jobs" line further down; don't lead with it.
3. **Sandbox backend matrix (`sandbox-exec`/`bwrap`/`docker`/`none`).** Belongs on a "how it works" or `doctor` page. On the homepage it triggers "do I have bwrap?" anxiety that distracts from the gate/attach story. Just say "platform-native sandbox by default."

## Honesty flags for the marketing copy

- The README line **"a watchdog the agent cannot fool"** is defensible under sandbox isolation of `gate/nonce` but is **not** cryptographic. If the sandbox were misconfigured to `--sandbox none`, the agent process could read the nonce file. Either keep the framing but qualify with "when the sandbox is enabled" (which it is by default), or soften to "a watchdog the agent process has no path to fool under the default sandbox." Don't claim crypto guarantees the code doesn't provide.
- The README's **"signed `dr-gate` marker"** is accurate as a process-isolation primitive; just don't imply HMAC/Ed25519.
- The chains section claims **"signed acceptance gate"** per step — true; each step is a real run that calls `run_acceptance_gate` + `validate_acceptance_marker`. Safe to repeat.

  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s-3);
  padding: 10px 14px;
  background: var(--term-bg-soft);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--term-edge);
}

.term-dots { display: inline-flex; gap: 6px; }
.term-dots span {
  width: 10px;
  height: 10px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--term-edge);
}

.term-title {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  color: var(--term-dim);
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
}

.term-body {
  padding: 18px 20px;
  overflow-x: auto;
  white-space: pre;
}

.term-body .prompt { color: var(--term-green); }
.term-body .you { color: var(--term-fg); }
.term-body .out { color: var(--term-dim); }
.term-body .ok { color: var(--term-green); }
.term-body .warn { color: var(--term-amber); }
.term-body .fail { color: var(--term-red); }
.term-body .meta { color: var(--term-dim); font-style: italic; }
.term-body .accent { color: var(--term-green); }
.term-body .cursor {
  display: inline-block;
  width: 0.55ch;
  background: var(--term-green);
  animation: blink 1.05s steps(1, end) infinite;
}

@keyframes blink {
  50% { background: transparent; }
}

/* ============================================
   QUICKSTART (4-line demo)
   ============================================ */

.quickstart {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1.1fr);
  gap: clamp(var(--s-5), 4vw, var(--s-7));
  align-items: start;
}

@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .quickstart { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
}

.quickstart-steps {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--s-5);
}

.qs-step {
  border-left: 2px solid var(--bone-edge);
  padding-left: var(--s-5);
}

.qs-step strong {
  display: block;
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  letter-spacing: 0.15em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--signal-ink);
  margin-bottom: var(--s-2);
}

.qs-step p {
  color: var(--ink-soft);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  line-height: 1.55;
}

/* ============================================
   MENTAL MODEL DIAGRAM
   ============================================ */

.diagram {
  background: var(--bone-deep);
  border: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  padding: clamp(var(--s-5), 4vw, var(--s-7));
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  line-height: 1.75;
  white-space: pre;
  overflow-x: auto;
  color: var(--ink-soft);
}

.diagram .node {
  background: var(--bone);
  border: 1px solid var(--ink);
  padding: 4px 10px;
  color: var(--ink);
  display: inline-block;
}

.diagram .gate {
  border-color: var(--signal-deep);
  background: var(--signal-wash);
  color: var(--signal-ink);
}

.diagram .note { color: var(--ash); }
.diagram .arrow { color: var(--ash-mute); }

/* ============================================
   CAPABILITIES (long-form, one demo each)
   ============================================ */

.cap {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 5fr) minmax(0, 7fr);
  gap: clamp(var(--s-6), 6vw, var(--s-8));
  align-items: center;
  padding-block: clamp(var(--s-7), 7vw, var(--s-9));
  border-top: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
}

.cap:first-of-type { border-top: 0; }

.cap--flip { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 7fr) minmax(0, 5fr); }
.cap--flip .cap-body { order: 2; }
.cap--flip .cap-visual { order: 1; }

@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .cap, .cap--flip { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
  .cap--flip .cap-body { order: unset; }
  .cap--flip .cap-visual { order: unset; }
}

.cap-num {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  letter-spacing: 0.15em;
  color: var(--ash);
}

.cap-title {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: var(--fs-h2);
  font-weight: 500;
  letter-spacing: -0.02em;
  line-height: 1.1;
  color: var(--ink);
  margin-block: var(--s-3) var(--s-4);
}

.cap-body p {
  color: var(--ink-soft);
  font-size: 1.0625rem;
  line-height: 1.6;
  max-width: 52ch;
}

.cap-body p + p { margin-top: var(--s-4); }

.cap-body code {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: 0.95em;
  background: var(--bone-deep);
  border: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  padding: 1px 6px;
  color: var(--ink);
}

.cap-meta {
  margin-top: var(--s-5);
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  color: var(--ash);
}
.cap-meta b { color: var(--signal-ink); font-weight: 500; }

/* ============================================
   COMPARISON TABLE
   ============================================ */

.compare {
  width: 100%;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
}

.compare th,
.compare td {
  text-align: left;
  padding: var(--s-4) var(--s-4);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  vertical-align: top;
}

.compare th {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  letter-spacing: 0.12em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ash);
  font-weight: 500;
  padding-bottom: var(--s-3);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ink);
}

.compare td:first-child {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  color: var(--ink);
  width: 28%;
}

.compare td.dr {
  color: var(--ink);
  background: var(--signal-wash);
}

.compare td.dr b { color: var(--signal-ink); font-weight: 600; }

.compare td.bare { color: var(--ash); }

@media (max-width: 720px) {
  .compare th, .compare td { padding: var(--s-3); font-size: var(--fs-xs); }
}

/* ============================================
   PROVIDERS
   ============================================ */

.providers {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr));
  gap: 0;
  border: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
}

.provider {
  padding: var(--s-5) var(--s-5);
  border-right: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--s-2);
}

.provider:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.provider:nth-last-child(-n+3) { border-bottom: 0; }

.provider-kind {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  letter-spacing: 0.12em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ash);
}

.provider-name {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: 1.0625rem;
  color: var(--ink);
}

.provider-id {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  color: var(--signal-ink);
}

@media (max-width: 720px) {
  .providers { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }
  .provider { border-right: 1px solid var(--bone-edge) !important; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bone-edge) !important; }
}

/* ============================================
   FAQ
   ============================================ */

.faq-list {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
}

.faq-item {
  border-top: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  padding: var(--s-5) 0;
}

.faq-item:last-child { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bone-edge); }

.faq-q {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: 1.125rem;
  color: var(--ink);
  margin-bottom: var(--s-3);
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
}

.faq-a {
  color: var(--ink-soft);
  max-width: var(--w-prose);
  line-height: 1.6;
}

.faq-a code {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: 0.92em;
  background: var(--bone-deep);
  border: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  padding: 1px 6px;
}

/* ============================================
   FOOTER
   ============================================ */

.site-footer {
  border-top: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  background: var(--bone-deep);
  padding-block: var(--s-7) var(--s-6);
}

.footer-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 2fr repeat(3, 1fr);
  gap: var(--s-6);
}

@media (max-width: 720px) {
  .footer-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }
}

.footer-brand {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--s-3);
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-weight: 500;
  color: var(--ink);
}

.footer-tag {
  margin-top: var(--s-3);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--ash);
  max-width: 36ch;
}

.footer-col h4 {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  letter-spacing: 0.15em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ash);
  margin-bottom: var(--s-3);
  font-weight: 500;
}

.footer-col ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--s-2); }
.footer-col a {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--ink-soft);
  transition: color var(--t-fast);
}
.footer-col a:hover { color: var(--signal-ink); }

.footer-fine {
  margin-top: var(--s-7);
  padding-top: var(--s-5);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--bone-edge);
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  color: var(--ash);
  letter-spacing: 0.05em;
}

@media (max-width: 540px) {
  .footer-fine { flex-direction: column; gap: var(--s-2); }
}

/* ============================================
   UTILITIES
   ============================================ */

.kicker {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  letter-spacing: 0.15em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ash);
}

.divider-rule {
  height: 1px;
  background: var(--bone-edge);
  border: 0;
  margin-block: var(--s-6);
}

.mark {
  background: var(--signal-wash);
  padding: 0 0.2em;
  color: var(--ink);
}

.flare {
  color: var(--flare-deep);
  font-weight: 600;
}

.reveal {
  opacity: 0;
  transform: translateY(16px);
  transition: opacity var(--t-slow) var(--ease), transform var(--t-slow) var(--ease);
}

.reveal.is-visible {
  opacity: 1;
  transform: none;
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration: 0.001ms !important;
    transition-duration: 0.001ms !important;
  }
  .reveal { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
}

import Header from '../components/Header.astro';
import Footer from '../components/Footer.astro';
import '../styles/tokens.css';
import '../styles/main.css';

interface Props {
  title: string;
  description?: string;
  canonicalPath?: string;
  ogImage?: string;
  noIndex?: boolean;
}

const {
  title,
  description = 'A harness around the agent CLI you already use. Isolated runs, signed acceptance, durable state, undo, audit trail.',
  canonicalPath,
  ogImage = '/assets/deadreckon-logo.png',
  noIndex = false,
} = Astro.props;

const site = 'https://deadreckon.dev';
const canonical = canonicalPath ? `${site}${canonicalPath}` : site;
---
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>{title}</title>
  <meta name="description" content={description} />
  <meta name="theme-color" content="#f4f0e6" />
  {noIndex && <meta name="robots" content="noindex" />}
  <link rel="canonical" href={canonical} />
  <link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="/assets/deadreckon-icon.png" />

  <meta property="og:type" content="website" />
  <meta property="og:url" content={canonical} />
  <meta property="og:title" content={title} />
  <meta property="og:description" content={description} />
  <meta property="og:image" content={`${site}${ogImage}`} />
  <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
  <meta name="twitter:title" content={title} />
  <meta name="twitter:description" content={description} />
  <meta name="twitter:image" content={`${site}${ogImage}`} />

  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
  <link
    href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600&display=swap"
    rel="stylesheet"
  />
</head>
<body>
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
  <Header />
  <main id="main">
    <slot />
  </main>
  <Footer />

  <script is:inline>
    // Reveal-on-scroll
    const io = new IntersectionObserver(
      (entries) => {
        for (const e of entries) {
          if (e.isIntersecting) {
            e.target.classList.add('is-visible');
            io.unobserve(e.target);
          }
        }
      },
      { threshold: 0.1, rootMargin: '0px 0px -10% 0px' }
    );
    for (const el of document.querySelectorAll('.reveal')) io.observe(el);

    // Copy buttons
    for (const btn of document.querySelectorAll('[data-copy]')) {
      btn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
        const text = btn.getAttribute('data-copy') || '';
        try {
          await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
          const prev = btn.textContent;
          btn.textContent = 'Copied';
          btn.classList.add('copied');
          setTimeout(() => {
            btn.textContent = prev;
            btn.classList.remove('copied');
          }, 1400);
        } catch (_) {}
      });
    }
  </script>

  <style is:global>
    .skip-link {
      position: absolute;
      left: -9999px;
      top: 0;
      background: var(--ink);
      color: var(--bone);
      padding: 8px 12px;
      font-family: var(--font-mono);
      font-size: 0.875rem;
      z-index: 100;
    }
    .skip-link:focus { left: 12px; top: 12px; }
  </style>
</body>
</html>

<span class="meta">  (detaches automatically; close this terminal whenever you want)</span>

<span class="meta"># ...two hours later, different laptop...</span>

<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon attach latest</span>
<span class="out">  turn 14/?  spend $4.18  acceptance </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰ 5/5 passed</span>
<span class="out">  gate       </span><span class="ok">marker signed · run ready to promote</span>
<span class="out">  artifact   </span>RUN-NARRATIVE.md · RUN-DECISIONS.md · provenance.jsonl<span class="cursor">&nbsp;</span>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  {/* ============================================ THE FORGERY DEMO ============================================ */}
  <section class="section" id="watchdog">
    <div class="wrap">
      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">The mechanic</span>
      <h2 class="section-title reveal">A separate process decides when the run is done. <em>The agent is not in the room.</em></h2>
      <p class="section-lead reveal">
        Every unattended-agent product runs into the same problem: the agent decides when it's
        finished. The transcript looks confident. The tests aren't run. You shipped a lie.
        deadreckon fixes this with a 33-line companion binary, <code>dr-gate</code>, that runs
        outside the agent's sandbox and signs the result. The marker is what unlocks promotion.
        The agent has no path to produce it.
      </p>

      <div class="quickstart">
        <div class="term reveal" aria-label="The dr-gate watchdog rejecting a forged marker">
          <div class="term-bar">
            <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
            <span class="term-title">dr-gate · watchdog</span>
          </div>
          <div class="term-body">
<span class="meta"># inside the run's sandbox</span>
<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">cat /run/gate/nonce</span>
<span class="fail">cat: /run/gate/nonce: Permission denied</span>

<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">echo '&#123;"accepted":true&#125;'</span> &gt; proofs/turn-acceptance.json
<span class="prompt">agent$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon finish latest</span>
<span class="fail">refused: marker signature missing</span>
<span class="fail">       expected: nonce-derived hash; got: empty</span>

<span class="meta"># meanwhile, outside the sandbox</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">dr-gate sign</span>
<span class="out">  read    </span>$RUN/gate/nonce <span class="ok">(0600, root-owned for this run)</span>
<span class="out">  hashed  </span>nonce + marker fields
<span class="out">  wrote   </span>proofs/turn-acceptance.json
<span class="ok">  signed ✓</span>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="quickstart-steps reveal">
          <div class="qs-step">
            <strong>01 · Isolated nonce</strong>
            <p>
              At run start, deadreckon writes a UUID nonce to <code>gate/nonce</code> outside the
              agent's sandbox root. The agent process has no read path to it.
            </p>
          </div>
          <div class="qs-step">
            <strong>02 · Out-of-band signature</strong>
            <p>
              <code>dr-gate</code> is a separate binary. It reads the nonce, hashes it with the
              acceptance fields, and writes the marker to <code>proofs/turn-acceptance.json</code>.
            </p>
          </div>
          <div class="qs-step">
            <strong>03 · Refusal by default</strong>
            <p>
              The main binary verifies the marker against the nonce before promotion. No valid
              signature, no promotion. The run loops, the agent gets another turn.
            </p>
          </div>
          <div class="qs-step">
            <strong>Honest scope</strong>
            <p>
              The signature is a hash, not an HMAC. The security property is process isolation
              under the default sandbox (<code>sandbox-exec</code> on macOS,
              <code>bwrap</code> on Linux), not cryptography. Turn the sandbox off, you lose the
              guarantee.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  {/* ============================================ MENTAL MODEL ============================================ */}
  <section class="section" id="how">
    <div class="wrap">
      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">How it works</span>
      <h2 class="section-title reveal">The agent owns the coding. <em>deadreckon owns the boundary.</em></h2>

      <div class="diagram reveal" aria-label="Mental model: repo to worktree to signed gate to artifact">
{`  your repo (untouched)
        │
        │  deadreckon done  "what 'finished' looks like, in English"
        │  deadreckon run   "what to build"
        ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  isolated worktree on  dr/...  branch                       │
  │  ~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<run-id>/                  │
  │                                                             │
  │   provider route ────►  cli:codex · cli:claude-code         │
  │                         anthropic · openai · smoke          │
  │                                                             │
  │   each turn: events.jsonl · spend.jsonl · traces.jsonl      │
  │              provenance.jsonl · snapshots/turn-N/           │
  └────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           │ checks fail?  agent gets another turn
                           │ checks pass?  ask the watchdog
                           ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐`}
<span class="gate">{`  │  dr-gate (separate process · holds the nonce)               │
  │      reads gate/nonce  ·  signs proofs/turn-acceptance      │`}</span>
{`  └────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │ valid signature?
                           ▼
  promoted artifact
        RUN-NARRATIVE.md · RUN-DECISIONS.md · AS-BUILT-DELTA.md
        manifest.json · full provenance trail
        │
        │  deadreckon apply | export | extend | discard
        ▼
  your branch or library`}
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  {/* ============================================ CAPABILITIES ============================================ */}
  <section class="section" id="capabilities">
    <div class="wrap">
      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Capabilities</span>
      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Five things you can do that the agent CLI alone can't.</h2>

      <div class="cap reveal">
        <div class="cap-body">
          <span class="cap-num">01</span>
          <h3 class="cap-title">Your checkout is never touched.</h3>
          <p>
            In a git repo, <code>deadreckon run</code> opens a separate worktree on a
            <code>dr/...</code> branch under <code>~/.deadreckon/worktrees/</code>. The agent
            writes there. Your checkout sits exactly where you left it until you choose to merge:
          </p>
          <p>
            <code>deadreckon apply &lt;run-id&gt;</code>. Or <code>discard</code>. Or
            <code>export</code> the finished tree to a new directory and never touch your branch
            at all. Worktrees, snapshots, and the launch directory are recorded so resumes find
            their way back even after a crash.
          </p>
          <div class="cap-meta">Modes: <b>worktree (default)</b> · copy · fresh · in-place</div>
        </div>
        <div class="cap-visual">
          <div class="term">
            <div class="term-bar">
              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
              <span class="term-title">filesystem after `deadreckon run`</span>
            </div>
            <div class="term-body">
<span class="out">~/code/myapp/                </span><span class="ok">← your checkout, unchanged</span>
<span class="out">  src/...</span>
<span class="out">  .git/</span>

<span class="out">~/.deadreckon/worktrees/</span>
<span class="out">  myapp-m7q3-build-a1f2/      </span><span class="accent">← agent works here</span>
<span class="out">    src/...                   </span>(branch: dr/build-the-app)
<span class="out">    state.json</span>
<span class="out">    events.jsonl</span>
<span class="out">    spend.jsonl</span>
<span class="out">    snapshots/turn-1/ ... turn-N/</span>
<span class="out">    proofs/turn-acceptance.json</span>

<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">git -C ~/code/myapp status</span>
<span class="ok">nothing to commit, working tree clean</span>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="cap cap--flip reveal">
        <div class="cap-body">
          <span class="cap-num">02</span>
          <h3 class="cap-title">Attach from a different laptop, on a different day.</h3>
          <p>
            The run lives on disk, not in your terminal. Every turn writes
            <code>state.json</code>, <code>events.jsonl</code>, <code>traces.jsonl</code>,
            <code>spend.jsonl</code>, and a working-directory snapshot. Close the lid. Open the
            other Mac. Type <code>deadreckon attach latest</code>. The TUI replays where the run
            is, what it just edited, what it spent, and how many acceptance checks have passed.
          </p>
          <p>
            Ctrl-D detaches without killing the run. <code>kill</code> stops it cleanly.
            <code>resume</code> picks up from the last completed turn, ignoring partial trace
            entries.
          </p>
          <div class="cap-meta">Polling cadence: <b>events.jsonl every 500ms</b> · same-process bus when local</div>
        </div>
        <div class="cap-visual">
          <div class="term">
            <div class="term-bar">
              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
              <span class="term-title">deadreckon attach latest</span>
            </div>
            <div class="term-body">
<span class="out">┌─ run m7q3 · build the app ──────────────┐</span>
<span class="out">│ turn 14   wall 1h:42m   spend  $4.18   │</span>
<span class="out">│ provider  cli:codex     ctx 38% / 200k │</span>
<span class="out">├─ acceptance ───────────────────────────┤</span>
<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> cargo_test           passed       │</span>
<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> file_exists          passed       │</span>
<span class="out">│ </span><span class="ok">▰▰▰▰▰</span><span class="out"> content_match        passed       │</span>
<span class="out">│ </span><span class="warn">▰▰▰○○</span><span class="out"> build_success        running...   │</span>
<span class="out">├─ activity ─────────────────────────────┤</span>
<span class="out">│ 14:32 edit  src/auth/session.rs        │</span>
<span class="out">│ 14:33 edit  src/auth/mod.rs            │</span>
<span class="out">│ 14:33 run   cargo test --lib auth      │</span>
<span class="out">│ 14:35 </span><span class="accent">dr-gate signing marker...</span><span class="out">         │</span>
<span class="out">└────────────────────────────────────────┘</span>
<span class="meta">Ctrl-D detach · Ctrl-C never (use `deadreckon kill`)</span>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="cap reveal">
        <div class="cap-body">
          <span class="cap-num">03</span>
          <h3 class="cap-title">Undo turn 7. Keep turns 1 through 6.</h3>
          <p>
            Snapshots happen at turn boundaries, on disk, independent of git. So you can rewind
            a single bad turn without rolling back the whole run or rewriting branch history.
            The undo itself is recorded in <code>traces.jsonl</code>; the rest of the run keeps
            going.
          </p>
          <p>
            This is not <code>git reset</code> with extra steps. It works on the run's own snapshot
            trail, which means it works on <code>--in-place</code> runs in dirty repos and on
            non-git working directories too.
          </p>
        </div>
        <div class="cap-visual">
          <div class="term">
            <div class="term-bar">
              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
              <span class="term-title">deadreckon undo --turn 7</span>
            </div>
            <div class="term-body">
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon undo --run m7q3 --turn 7</span>
<span class="out">  restoring  </span>snapshots/turn-6/ <span class="ok">(working dir)</span>
<span class="out">  trace      </span>logged: undo-from=7 to=6
<span class="out">  state      </span>head turn now 6 · history preserved
<span class="ok">  done.</span> resume with: deadreckon resume m7q3

<span class="meta"># turns 1-6 still in history, snapshots still on disk</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">ls snapshots/</span>
<span class="out">turn-1  turn-2  turn-3  turn-4  turn-5  turn-6  turn-7</span>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="cap cap--flip reveal">
        <div class="cap-body">
          <span class="cap-num">04</span>
          <h3 class="cap-title">Get a reviewable artifact, not a chat log.</h3>
          <p>
            deadreckon records which model call touched which files in
            <code>provenance.jsonl</code>. When the gate signs off, it writes a narrative,
            a decisions log, and a file-lineage manifest. You read the artifact. You don't
            scroll a 4,000-line transcript trying to figure out what the model actually did.
          </p>
          <p>
            <code>deadreckon doc &lt;run-id&gt; --kind delta</code> proposes architecture-doc
            updates when the run was broad enough to need them. That's how you keep
            <code>AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md</code> honest after a long agentic week.
          </p>
          <div class="cap-meta">Outputs: <b>RUN-NARRATIVE</b> · RUN-DECISIONS · RUN-AS-BUILT · AS-BUILT-DELTA · manifest.json</div>
        </div>
        <div class="cap-visual">
          <div class="term">
            <div class="term-bar">
              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
              <span class="term-title">RUN-NARRATIVE.md (excerpt)</span>
            </div>
            <div class="term-body">
<span class="out">## What changed</span>

<span class="out">Added password-based signup, login, and a saved-drawing</span>
<span class="out">route. New routes live in </span><span class="accent">src/auth/</span><span class="out"> and </span><span class="accent">src/drawings/</span><span class="out">.</span>

<span class="out">## Why</span>

<span class="out">The acceptance spec asked for three flows. Turn 4</span>
<span class="out">discovered an existing `User` model in `src/db/users.rs`</span>
<span class="out">and reused it instead of adding a parallel table.</span>

<span class="out">## Files touched (provenance.jsonl summary)</span>

<span class="out">  src/auth/session.rs       turns 3, 5, 7, 9</span>
<span class="out">  src/auth/mod.rs           turns 3, 9</span>
<span class="out">  src/drawings/save.rs      turns 11, 12</span>
<span class="out">  migrations/0004_auth.sql  turn 3</span>
<span class="out">  tests/auth_test.rs        turns 6, 8, 10</span>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="cap reveal">
        <div class="cap-body">
          <span class="cap-num">05</span>
          <h3 class="cap-title">Cap the spend. Cap the wall clock. Walk away.</h3>
          <p>
            Every provider response appends a record to <code>spend.jsonl</code> and updates the
            run total. Direct API routes (Anthropic, OpenAI) track dollar cost.
            Subscription CLI routes (Claude Code, Codex) cap by wall-clock time, since the
            subscription already paid the bill.
          </p>
          <p>
            Pass <code>--max-spend 15</code> or <code>--max-wall-seconds 1800</code> and the run
            stops itself at the cap. Cross a high-spend threshold without the flag and you get
            an explicit confirmation, so a script doesn't accidentally launch a $200 run.
          </p>
        </div>
        <div class="cap-visual">
          <div class="term">
            <div class="term-bar">
              <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
              <span class="term-title">deadreckon run --max-spend 15</span>
            </div>
            <div class="term-body">
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-spend 15</span>
<span class="out">  spend cap     </span>$15.00
<span class="out">  wall cap      </span>none
<span class="out">  current spend </span>$0.00
<span class="out">  starting...</span>

<span class="meta">...later...</span>
<span class="out">  turn 22 · spend $14.82 / $15.00</span>
<span class="warn">  cap reached after turn 22</span>
<span class="ok">  run paused cleanly · resume with: deadreckon resume latest</span>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  {/* ============================================ COMPARE ============================================ */}
  <section class="section" id="compare">
    <div class="wrap">
      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Compared</span>
      <h2 class="section-title reveal">deadreckon doesn't replace your agent CLI. <em>It supervises it.</em></h2>
      <p class="section-lead reveal">
        Use the agent CLI you already trust for the coding. Use deadreckon for the parts the
        agent CLI was never designed to do: isolation, evidence, recovery, and a "done" you can
        defend.
      </p>

      <table class="compare reveal" aria-label="Comparison with running the agent CLI directly">
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>Operational concern</th>
            <th>Agent CLI alone</th>
            <th>deadreckon supervising the CLI</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr>
            <td>Workspace safety</td>
            <td class="bare">Runs where you start it</td>
            <td class="dr">Isolated worktree by default. <b>Your checkout sits untouched until you say apply.</b></td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Long-running attach</td>
            <td class="bare">Tied to the current terminal</td>
            <td class="dr">Run state is durable. <b>Attach from another machine the next day.</b></td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Spend control</td>
            <td class="bare">Visibility varies by provider</td>
            <td class="dr"><b>spend.jsonl per turn.</b> Hard caps on dollars or wall-clock.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Undo</td>
            <td class="bare">Manual git, if it works</td>
            <td class="dr"><b>Snapshots every turn.</b> Restore turn 7 without losing 1–6.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Provenance</td>
            <td class="bare">Transcript doesn't map cleanly to files</td>
            <td class="dr">Model/tool/file linkage written to <b>provenance.jsonl</b>.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>"Done" criteria</td>
            <td class="bare">The agent declares itself done</td>
            <td class="dr"><b>Out-of-process watchdog signs.</b> No marker, no promotion.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Applying the work</td>
            <td class="bare">Tool-specific patch flow</td>
            <td class="dr"><b>apply · discard · export · extend</b> as first-class verbs.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Multi-run coordination</td>
            <td class="bare">Left to the operator</td>
            <td class="dr">Scope/task locks prevent conflicting same-task runs.</td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  </section>

  {/* ============================================ TRY ============================================ */}
  <section class="section" id="try">
    <div class="wrap">
      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Try without keys</span>
      <h2 class="section-title reveal">30 seconds. No API key. <em>Real loop, real gate, fake model.</em></h2>
      <p class="section-lead reveal">
        Smoke mode fakes the provider response. Every other moving part is real: the worktree,
        the sandbox, the snapshots, the spend ledger, the watchdog signing the marker. Use it
        to verify the loop on your machine before pointing real money at it.
      </p>

      <div class="term reveal">

  {/* ============================================ INSTALL ============================================ */}
  <section class="section" id="install">
    <div class="wrap">
      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">Install</span>
      <h2 class="section-title reveal">One binary. Build it once, alias it, walk away.</h2>

      <div class="quickstart reveal">
        <div class="term">
          <div class="term-bar">
            <span class="term-dots"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
            <span class="term-title">install · configure · run</span>
          </div>
          <div class="term-body">
<span class="meta"># build from source (alpha, no crate yet)</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">git clone https://github.com/deadreckon/deadreckon</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">cd deadreckon &amp;&amp; cargo build --release</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">./target/release/deadreckon completion install</span>

<span class="meta"># pick a provider</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon init --provider cli:claude-code --sandbox auto --max-spend 10</span>

<span class="meta"># declare done in English</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon done "users can sign up, log in, save a drawing"</span>

<span class="meta"># go</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon run "build the app"</span>
<span class="prompt">$</span> <span class="you">deadreckon attach latest</span>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="quickstart-steps">
          <div class="qs-step">
            <strong>Requirements</strong>
            <p>Rust 1.75+ to build. macOS or Linux for the native sandbox. A provider seat or API key, or run with <code>--smoke</code>.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="qs-step">
            <strong>Sandbox</strong>
            <p><code>sandbox-exec</code> on macOS, <code>bwrap</code> on Linux, opt-in <code>docker</code>, <code>none</code> if you really know what you're doing.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="qs-step">
            <strong>State on disk</strong>
            <p>Everything writes under <code>~/.deadreckon/</code>. Set <code>DEADRECKON_HOME</code> for sandbox-isolated tests.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="qs-step">
            <strong>Verify it works</strong>
            <p><code>deadreckon doctor</code> checks config, providers, sandbox backends, disk, and runtime in one command.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  {/* ============================================ NAME ============================================ */}
  <section class="section" id="name">
    <div class="wrap">
      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">The name</span>
      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Dead reckoning. <em>Navigation without perfect visibility.</em></h2>
      <p class="section-lead reveal">
        Sailors plotted dead reckoning when the stars were out of view. Track every move so you
        know where you are now. Long unattended agent runs face the same problem: partial context,
        a terminal that may be gone when you look back, a model that may have lied at turn 7.
        Don't trust the final answer. Navigate by evidence.
      </p>
      <p class="section-lead reveal">
        The questions deadreckon exists to answer:
      </p>
      <ul class="reveal" style="list-style:none; padding:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:var(--s-3); font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--fs-sm); color: var(--ink-soft);">
        <li>→ Where did the agent run, and what did it spend?</li>
        <li>→ Can I attach after closing my laptop?</li>
        <li>→ Can I undo turn 7 without rolling back the whole project?</li>
        <li>→ Can I prove the agent didn't mark its own work as accepted?</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </section>

  {/* ============================================ FAQ ============================================ */}
  <section class="section" id="faq">
    <div class="wrap">
      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">FAQ</span>
      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Honest answers, including the ones that make this look smaller.</h2>

      <div class="faq-list reveal">
        <div class="faq-item">
          <h3 class="faq-q">Does deadreckon replace Claude Code or Codex?</h3>
          <p class="faq-a">No. You still install the CLI you already use. deadreckon shells out to it, runs it inside an isolated worktree under a sandbox, and supervises the loop around it. The agent does the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
          <h3 class="faq-q">Is the gate signature cryptographic?</h3>
          <p class="faq-a">No. The signature is a hash of the run nonce with the marker fields, written by a separate binary (<code>dr-gate</code>). The security property is filesystem isolation of <code>gate/nonce</code> under the default sandbox, not an HMAC or signing key. Run with <code>--sandbox none</code> and you lose the guarantee. This is documented honestly in the architecture notes; we'd rather you understand the scope than oversell it.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
          <h3 class="faq-q">What happens if the run crashes mid-turn?</h3>
          <p class="faq-a">The next <code>deadreckon resume</code> reads <code>events.jsonl</code> and <code>traces.jsonl</code>, ignores incomplete trailing entries, and restarts from the last completed turn. Snapshots are written at turn boundaries, so worst case you re-do one turn.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
          <h3 class="faq-q">Can I run more than one at a time?</h3>
          <p class="faq-a">Yes. Each run scopes to a project; scope and task locks prevent two runs from clobbering the same workspace. <code>deadreckon list</code> shows everything in the current project, <code>--all</code> shows everything everywhere.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
          <h3 class="faq-q">Does it work without a git repo?</h3>
          <p class="faq-a">Yes. Outside git, deadreckon falls back to copy mode (or <code>--in-place</code> if you insist). Worktrees are the default only when there's something to branch from.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
          <h3 class="faq-q">What's still rough?</h3>
          <p class="faq-a">deadreckon is alpha. <code>deadreckon import</code> from other tools' histories produces an inventory, not a deep normalization. Chains work but are deliberately tucked behind a separate subcommand. The Windows path isn't there yet; macOS and Linux are.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="faq-item">
          <h3 class="faq-q">Where does state live?</h3>
          <p class="faq-a">Under <code>~/.deadreckon/</code> by default. Per-run: <code>state.json</code>, <code>events.jsonl</code>, <code>traces.jsonl</code>, <code>spend.jsonl</code>, <code>provenance.jsonl</code>, <code>snapshots/turn-N/</code>, <code>proofs/turn-acceptance.json</code>. Accepted runs are promoted to <code>~/.deadreckon/library/&lt;scope&gt;/&lt;run-id&gt;/</code>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>
</Base>

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Convert term-body div to pre with balanced close tags

```bash
cd /Users/gdc/deadreckon-site && python3 <<'PY'
import re
path = 'src/pages/index.astro'
with open(path) as f:
    src = f.read()

# Find each <div class="term-body"> ... matching </div>
# We need to balance nested divs. Strategy: find every <div class="term-body"> and replace with <pre class="term-body">,
# then walk forward to find the matching </div> (counting nested <div> opens) and replace it with </pre>.

i = 0
out = []
n = len(src)
while i < n:
    m = re.match(r'<div class="term-body">', src[i:])
    if not m:
        out.append(src[i])
        i += 1
        continue
    out.append('<pre class="term-body">')
    j = i + m.end()
    depth = 1
    # walk to find matching close (counting <div tags inside)
    while j < n and depth > 0:
        if src[j:j+5] == '<div ' or src[j:j+5] == '<div>':
            depth += 1
            # advance past tag
            close = src.find('>', j)
            if close == -1: break
            out.append(src[j:close+1])
            j = close + 1
        elif src[j:j+6] == '</div>':
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                out.append('</pre>')
                j += 6
                break
            else:
                out.append('</div>')
                j += 6
        else:
            out.append(src[j])
            j += 1
    i = j

with open(path, 'w') as f:
    f.write(''.join(out))

print("pre opens:", sum(1 for _ in re.finditer(r'<pre class="term-body">', open(path).read())))
print("pre closes:", sum(1 for _ in re.finditer(r'</pre>', open(path).read())))
PY
```

```md
# deadreckon-site

Marketing site for [deadreckon](https://github.com/deadreckon/deadreckon), the
harness around the agent CLI you already use.

Built with Astro. Static output. One page so far; the page is the product
brief, the docs live in the deadreckon repo.

## Run it

\```bash
bun install
bun run dev      # local dev server on http://localhost:4321
bun run build    # static output to ./dist
\```

Use `pnpm` or `npm` if you prefer; the lockfile is bun's.

## Editorial rules

Copy follows the rules in `/Users/gdc/impeccable/STYLE.md` (no em dashes, no
"delve", no "seamless", no "let's dive in"). When you edit the page, read that
file first.

Two cardinal rules specific to this site:

1. **Don't oversell the watchdog.** The `dr-gate` signature is a hash plus
   filesystem isolation of the nonce, not crypto. Say so on the page and in
   the FAQ. The integrity story is real; the precise framing is what makes it
   trustworthy.
2. **Mention real commands, not hypothetical ones.** Every command in a code
   block should be one you can paste into a working deadreckon install.

## Structure

\```
src/
  layouts/Base.astro    one shared layout (header + footer)
  components/
    Header.astro        sticky top nav
    Footer.astro
  pages/
    index.astro         the whole homepage
  styles/
    tokens.css          colors, type, spacing, motion
    main.css            page-section styles
public/
  assets/               wordmark, icon, logo (copied from deadreckon repo)
\```

## Brand

- **Wordmark green** is the accent. Pulled from the deadreckon wordmark
  (`docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png` in the deadreckon repo).
- **Bone paper** is the background. Warm, low-contrast, easy on long reads.
- **JetBrains Mono** carries headings. The product is a CLI; the type should
  say so.
- **Inter** is the body. Workhorse.

If you change accent colors, change them in `tokens.css` (`--signal`,
`--signal-deep`, `--signal-ink`, `--signal-wash`) and audit the terminal
palette below — the green is shared between brand and terminal output.

Site is built and committed. Here's what landed:

**`/Users/gdc/deadreckon-site/`** — single-page Astro site, initial commit `6bcbd3b`.

**Page structure** (one long scroll, narrative beats from CLI hero → trust → comparison):
1. **Hero**: tagline + install + live terminal showing `done` → `run` → walk-away → `attach`.
2. **The watchdog**: the strongest visual on the page — a terminal showing the agent's `cat /run/gate/nonce` getting `Permission denied`, a forged marker getting refused, and `dr-gate` signing out-of-band. Side panel scopes the security claim honestly (filesystem isolation + hash, not crypto).
3. **Mental model**: ASCII diagram of repo → worktree → turn loop → dr-gate → artifact, lifted from the README and visually highlighted.
4. **Five capabilities**, lazygit-style long-form: isolated worktree, walk-away attach, per-turn undo, reviewable artifact, spend/wall caps.
5. **Compared with agent CLI alone**: 8-row table, signal-green highlights the deadreckon column.
6. **Providers**: 6-cell grid covering CLI, API, smoke.
7. **Try without keys**: the `--smoke` block verbatim from the README.
8. **Install**: build + init + run quickstart.
9. **The name**: "navigate by evidence."
10. **FAQ**: 7 questions, including "Is the gate signature cryptographic?" → "No," with the honest scope.

**Design language**: bone-paper background, JetBrains Mono headlines, Inter body, signal-mint accent from the wordmark, dark terminal blocks throughout. Editorial discipline from impeccable's STYLE.md (no em dashes, no banned marketing verbs).

**Two agents fed the work**: one researched 11 CLI homepages (bun, deno, uv, biome, lazygit, charm, etc.) and recommended the section list; the other audited the deadreckon codebase and flagged the gate-signature framing as the load-bearing honesty issue, which the FAQ now addresses head-on.

**Run it**: `cd /Users/gdc/deadreckon-site && bun run dev` then open `http://localhost:4321`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 04:32:23Z)**_

Here's a single prompt tuned to the site's palette and typographic system. Paste it straight into ChatGPT (4o or o-image, the gpt-image-1 backend follows text literally; longer specific prompts beat short stylish ones).

---

**Prompt:**

A wide horizontal technical schematic, 16:9 aspect ratio, drawn as a clean engineering blueprint on warm bone-paper. Style: precise, minimal, ops-blueprint, hairline strokes, mono labels, flat shapes, no shadows, no gradients, no glow, no 3D. Read it like a Jepsen architecture diagram or a Honeycomb infrastructure sketch.

**Palette, used exactly:**
- Background: warm bone paper, #FDFBF4 (slight visible paper grain ok, very subtle).
- Strokes and primary text: near-black ink, #14171A.
- Mid-grey for secondary labels and arrows: #6E7176.
- **One accent only:** a bright minty signal-green, #2EE89D, used solely on the `dr-gate` element and the signed-marker arrow. No other element uses the green.
- One small dark terminal panel inside the worktree box uses background #15171A with off-white text #F2EFE6 and the same green for prompts.

**Typography:** all labels in a monospace face (JetBrains Mono or similar). Lowercase preferred. Use varied weight: bold for box titles, regular for inline detail. No serif. No script. No swooshes.

**Composition, left-to-right, five labelled stations connected by clean hairline arrows:**

1. **YOUR REPO**, a small flat outlined rectangle at the far left, hairline border. Tiny grey label underneath: `untouched`. Branch icon (a minimal Y-fork glyph) inside.

2. **ISOLATED WORKTREE**, a larger flat outlined rectangle in the centre-left. Inside, stacked vertically as label rows in mono:
   - `~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<run-id>/`
   - `branch: dr/build-the-app`
   - then a horizontal divider, then a mini stack of file labels: `state.json`, `events.jsonl`, `spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, `snapshots/turn-N/`
   - then the small dark terminal panel I described, with three example lines: `$ deadreckon run "build the app"`, `turn 14 · spend $4.18`, `▰▰▰▰▰ 5/5 passed` (the bars and the dollar amount in green).

3. **TURN LOOP**, drawn as a small circular flow with two curved arrows, sitting between the worktree and the gate. Label: `agent turn → snapshot → check → repeat`. Mid-grey.

4. **dr-gate** (the trust mechanic), a flat outlined rectangle on the right side, **outlined in the green accent**, sitting *outside* the worktree box to make it visually clear it lives in a separate process. Title in bold green. Inside, in mono:
   - `holds gate/nonce (0600)`
   - `signs proofs/turn-acceptance.json`
   - `the agent process has no read path`
   A green hairline arrow runs from the loop into dr-gate labelled `checks passed?`, and a green hairline arrow runs from dr-gate to the artifact labelled `signed marker`.

5. **PROMOTED ARTIFACT**, a flat outlined rectangle at the far right. Inside, mono labels stacked: `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, `RUN-DECISIONS.md`, `RUN-AS-BUILT.md`, `manifest.json`, `provenance trail`. A tiny grey caption underneath: `inspect · apply · export · extend`.

**Top of the canvas, very small mono caption (mid-grey):**
`the agent owns the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.`

**Bottom of the canvas, very small mono caption (mid-grey):**
`navigate by evidence.`

**Strict don'ts:** no purple, no neon, no glassmorphism, no isometric perspective, no rounded plump cards, no Material-style elevation shadows, no AI-cliché abstract swooshes, no people, no laptops, no clouds, no robot iconography, no decorative dots or sparkle. No icon set look (Lucide, Material, Phosphor). Hand-drafted hairline shapes only.

**Output:** PNG, 1600×900 minimum, no border/frame, no title bar — the canvas IS the diagram.

---

**Notes on the prompt:**

- The single-accent rule (mint-green only on `dr-gate` and the signed-marker arrow) is what will make this image read as "the gate is the special thing." If the model spreads green everywhere it'll feel like marketing artwork. If you get a slop output, the fastest fix is to re-prompt with `(only the dr-gate element uses green; everything else is black ink on bone paper)` appended.
- If the first generation crowds the worktree box, ask for "less detail inside the worktree, the terminal panel can show only the first two lines."
- If the model produces an isometric 3D box, append: `the diagram is strictly 2D, plan view, no perspective.`
- The exact hex codes (`#FDFBF4`, `#14171A`, `#2EE89D`) match my site tokens, so the final image will drop into the page without needing color correction.

Once the image is generated, save it as `public/assets/how-it-works.png` and I'll swap it in to replace the ASCII diagram in the `#how` section.

_**User (2026-05-13 04:44:54Z)**_

difference between apache and mit license?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 04:44:57Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 04:45:09Z)**_

Short version: both are permissive (use it, modify it, ship it, even in closed-source products). They diverge on **patents** and **attribution paperwork**.

**MIT (very short, ~170 words)**
- Permission: do anything.
- Required: keep the copyright notice and the license text in copies.
- Patents: silent. No express grant, no termination clause.
- Trademark: silent.
- Modification disclosure: not required.
- Boilerplate burden: near-zero. One file, one copyright line.

**Apache 2.0 (longer, ~3,000 words)**
- Permission: do anything.
- Required: keep the copyright notice, the license text, AND a `NOTICE` file if upstream ships one.
- **Patents (the big one):** each contributor grants you a license to any patents they own that read on their contribution. If you sue any contributor for patent infringement on that code, your patent grant terminates automatically. MIT gives you no such shield.
- **Trademark:** explicitly does *not* grant rights to project names, logos, or marks.
- **Modification disclosure:** files you modify must carry "prominent notices" stating they changed.
- Compatible with GPLv3 (MIT is too) but not GPLv2.

**When each fits**

- **MIT** is the default for libraries that want maximum drop-in adoption with zero friction. Tiny utility crates, tutorials, marketing sites. The cost of compliance is one paragraph in your repo. The tradeoff: zero patent protection for either side. If a contributor later turns out to hold a patent on what they wrote, MIT doesn't stop them from suing you.
- **Apache 2.0** is the default for anything substantial that companies might depend on (compilers, runtimes, agent frameworks, deadreckon-shaped things). The patent grant is real money to a corporate legal team. The retaliation clause discourages patent trolling among contributors. The cost: every file change technically needs a notice; the boilerplate is heavier; redistributors have to deal with `NOTICE` files.

**For deadreckon specifically**: Apache-2.0 on the CLI is the right call — it's the kind of project a company might pull into a CI pipeline, so the explicit patent grant carries weight. MIT on the marketing site is also right — there's nothing patentable on a static site, and MIT keeps the friction minimal for anyone who wants to fork the layout.

**Practical compatibility note**: Apache-2.0 code can be re-licensed inside an MIT or BSD downstream as long as you preserve the Apache notices. The reverse (taking MIT code into an Apache project) is fine too. So splitting them the way we did doesn't create a compatibility headache between the two repos.

```bash
python3 <<'PY'
# Build the attach TUI box with exact monospace alignment.
# Inner width = 40 cells (everything between the two │ pillars).
W = 40

def line(content):
    pad = W - len(content)
    assert pad >= 0, f"line too long ({len(content)} > {W}): {content!r}"
    return f"│{content}{' '*pad}│"

def divider(label=None):
    if label is None:
        return "├" + "─"*W + "┤"
    s = f"─ {label} "
    return "├" + s + "─"*(W - len(s)) + "┤"

def header(label):
    s = f"─ {label} "
    return "┌" + s + "─"*(W - len(s)) + "┐"

def footer():
    return "└" + "─"*W + "┘"

def cap_row(bar, name, status):
    # ▰▰▰▰▰  cargo_test            passed
    # bar 5, name padded to 15, status padded to (W - 5 - 1 - 1 - 15 - 1) ...
    # layout: " {bar} {name:15} {status}"   total cells = 1+5+1+15+1+len(status)
    # available for status = W - (1+5+1+15+1) = W - 23 = 17
    return f" {bar} {name:<15} {status:<17}"

def act_row(t, kind, body):
    # " {t}  {kind:5} {body}"
    # = 1 + 5 + 2 + 5 + 1 + len(body) = 14 + len(body), pad body to W-14
    return f" {t}  {kind:<5} {body:<{W-14}}"

box = []
box.append(header("run m7q3 · build the app"))
box.append(line(" turn 14   wall 1h:42m   spend  $4.18  "))
box.append(line(" provider  cli:codex     ctx 38% / 200k"))
box.append(divider("acceptance"))
box.append(line(cap_row("▰▰▰▰▰", "cargo_test",    "passed")))
box.append(line(cap_row("▰▰▰▰▰", "file_exists",   "passed")))
box.append(line(cap_row("▰▰▰▰▰", "content_match", "passed")))
box.append(line(cap_row("▰▰▰▱▱", "build_success", "running...")))
box.append(divider("activity"))
box.append(line(act_row("14:32", "edit", "src/auth/session.rs")))
box.append(line(act_row("14:33", "edit", "src/auth/mod.rs")))
box.append(line(act_row("14:33", "run",  "cargo test --lib auth")))
box.append(line(act_row("14:35", "",     "dr-gate signing marker...")))
box.append(footer())

for L in box:
    print(f"{len(L):3d}  {L}")
PY
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 04:50:36Z)**_

Commit `81fe982`. Three fixes landed:

1. **Box width**: five rows were 43 cells while the rest were 42, drifting the right pillar. Regenerated every line at a fixed inner width of 40 (total 42) via a Python pass. All 14 lines now report identical lengths.
2. **Mismatched glyphs**: the progress bars mixed `▰▰▰▰▰` (filled rectangle) with `▰▰▰○○` (rectangle + circle). Swapped the circles for `▱` U+25B1, the matching unfilled rectangle, so the bar reads as one continuous strip.
3. **JetBrains Mono ligatures**: `--lib` was rendering as `—lib` everywhere. Added `font-variant-ligatures: none` plus `font-feature-settings: 'liga' 0, 'calt' 0` to `.term-body`. This fixes `--`, `!=`, `->`, `==`, etc. across all nine terminal blocks on the page, not just this one.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 04:54:49Z)**_

A few gaps worth flagging before this ships. Ordered roughly by what would embarrass you fastest if a stranger landed on the page.

**Honesty / accuracy**

1. The hero install pill says `cargo install deadreckon`. That doesn't work today. The README in the CLI repo is explicit: "build from source (alpha, no crate yet)" and the install section there is `git clone … && cargo build --release`. The site is currently lying. I'd either match the README and change the pill to a git-clone-and-build command, or hide the pill until the crate is published.
2. The Capability #5 terminal claims the run "pauses cleanly" at the spend cap and you can `deadreckon resume latest`. I didn't verify this against the actual `--max-spend` codepath. If it actually kills the run instead of pausing, copy needs adjustment. Worth a 30-second grep in the deadreckon repo.

**Page weight**

3. `public/assets/diagram.jpeg` is 1.9 MB. That's the heaviest single asset on the page by an order of magnitude. A `magick … -quality 82 -strip` pass plus a `webp` sibling would drop it under 250 KB without visible loss. The other PNGs (icon 865 KB, logo 875 KB) are also bigger than they need to be for what's displayed.

**Social / preview**

4. OG image is set to `deadreckon-logo.png` which is 1448×1086 (4:3). Twitter/X and most unfurl previews want 1200×630. The current image will get center-cropped weirdly. Should generate a proper OG card, or at minimum re-export the logo padded into 1200×630 on bone background.
5. No JSON-LD/SoftwareApplication structured data. Minor SEO miss, not blocking.

**Infra hygiene**

6. No git remote yet, no push. `gh repo create gregce/deadreckon-site` plus a push would get this online via Pages or Vercel in five minutes.
7. No `robots.txt` and no `sitemap.xml`. One page, low stakes, but trivial to add. Astro has an integration.
8. No 404 page. Astro defaults to a generic one. A matching `src/pages/404.astro` is one of the lowest-effort polish wins.
9. Fonts load from Google's CDN. That's a third-party hop and a privacy footnote. Self-hosting JetBrains Mono and Inter is straightforward and shaves ~80 ms.

**Responsiveness**

10. I never tested below ~960 px. The hero grid collapses to single column, but the terminals' fixed character widths could still spill on narrow phones. Worth one Playwright pass at 375 px before publishing.

**Tiny consistency things**

11. The header GitHub button reads `GitHub →` but the footer "Project › GitHub" link has no arrow. Either both or neither.
12. The "Try without keys" section still references `deadreckon doc latest`, which is real, but the example output shows three files. If a smoke run produces a different set of files, the copy will drift over time.

**Nice-to-haves I'd consciously skip**

- Animated `.cast` demo via asciinema-player. The static terminals already carry the page. Animation buys a 1.5 MB JS bundle and one more thing to maintain.
- Dark mode. The dark terminal blocks already give the page enough chiaroscuro; a full dark variant is busywork at this stage.

Pick whichever of the top three (install honesty, image weight, push to a remote) feels most urgent and I'll do them.

77	    );

82	      btn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
83	        const text = btn.getAttribute('data-copy') || '';
84	        try {
85	          await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
86	          const prev = btn.textContent;
87	          btn.textContent = 'Copied';
88	          btn.classList.add('copied');
89	          setTimeout(() => {
90	            btn.textContent = prev;
91	            btn.classList.remove('copied');
92	          }, 1400);
93	        } catch (_) {}
94	      });
95	    }
96	  </script>

// Internal: render-and-screenshot for the OG card. Deleted after capture.
import '@fontsource/inter/400.css';
import '@fontsource/inter/600.css';

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8" />
  <title>OG render</title>
  <style>
    html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; background: #FDFBF4; }
    astro-dev-toolbar, astro-dev-overlay { display: none !important; }
    .card {
      width: 1200px;
      height: 630px;
      background: #FDFBF4;
      color: #14171A;
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace;
      position: relative;
      padding: 72px;
      box-sizing: border-box;
      display: flex;
      flex-direction: column;
      justify-content: space-between;
    }
    .top { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 18px; }
    .top img { height: 56px; width: auto; display: block; }
    .pill {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 10px;
      padding: 8px 14px;
      border: 1.5px solid #2E7A57;
      background: rgba(46, 232, 157, 0.18);
      color: #2E7A57;
      font-size: 16px;
      letter-spacing: 0.15em;
      text-transform: uppercase;
      font-weight: 500;
    }
    .pill::before {
      content: '';
      width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%;
      background: #2EE89D;
    }
    .title {
      font-size: 76px;
      font-weight: 500;
      line-height: 1.02;
      letter-spacing: -0.035em;
      max-width: 18ch;
    }
    .accent { color: #2E7A57; }
    .foot {
      display: flex;
      justify-content: space-between;
      align-items: flex-end;
      font-size: 18px;
      color: #6E7176;
      letter-spacing: 0.05em;
    }
    .foot .rule {
      flex: 1;
      margin-inline: 24px;
      height: 1px;
      background: #2EE89D;
      align-self: center;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <div class="card" id="card">
    <div class="top">
      <img src="/assets/deadreckon-wordmark-transparent.png" alt="" />
      <span class="pill">v0.x alpha</span>
    </div>
    <h1 class="title">walk away from your coding agent.<br/><span class="accent">come back to evidence.</span></h1>
    <div class="foot">
      <span>deadreckon.sh</span>
      <span class="rule"></span>
      <span>open source · Apache-2.0</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</body>
</html>

644	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Dead reckoning. <em>Navigation without perfect visibility.</em></h2>

646	        Sailors plotted dead reckoning when the stars were out of view. Track every move so you

656	        <li>→ Can I attach after closing the terminal?</li>

658	        <li>→ Can I prove the agent didn't mark its own work as accepted?</li>

664	  <section class="section" id="faq">
665	    <div class="wrap">
666	      <span class="section-eyebrow reveal">FAQ</span>
667	      <h2 class="section-title reveal">Honest answers, including the ones that make this look smaller.</h2>
668	
669	      <div class="faq-list reveal">
670	        <div class="faq-item">
671	          <h3 class="faq-q">Does deadreckon replace Claude Code or Codex?</h3>
672	          <p class="faq-a">No. You still install the CLI you already use. deadreckon shells out to it, runs it inside an isolated worktree under a sandbox, and supervises the loop around it. The agent does the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.</p>
673	        </div>
674	
675	        <div class="faq-item">
676	          <h3 class="faq-q">Is the gate signature cryptographic?</h3>
677	          <p class="faq-a">No. The signature is a hash of the run nonce with the marker fields, written by a separate binary (<code>dr-gate</code>). The security property is filesystem isolation of <code>gate/nonce</code> under the default sandbox, not an HMAC or signing key. Run with <code>--sandbox none</code> and you lose the guarantee. This is documented honestly in the architecture notes; we'd rather you understand the scope than oversell it.</p>
678	        </div>
679	
680	        <div class="faq-item">
681	          <h3 class="faq-q">What happens if the run crashes mid-turn?</h3>
682	          <p class="faq-a">The next <code>deadreckon resume</code> reads <code>events.jsonl</code> and <code>traces.jsonl</code>, ignores incomplete trailing entries, and restarts from the last completed turn. Snapshots are written at turn boundaries, so worst case you re-do one turn.</p>
683	        </div>
684	
685	        <div class="faq-item">
686	          <h3 class="faq-q">Can I run more than one at a time?</h3>
687	          <p class="faq-a">Yes. Each run scopes to a project; scope and task locks prevent two runs from clobbering the same workspace. <code>deadreckon list</code> shows everything in the current project, <code>--all</code> shows everything everywhere.</p>
688	        </div>
689
